title: Annotatio III §.X (2): Adversatur Analogia fidei — body-nature articles; forged miracles worsen the clash
pass_a_gloss: (2.) To the divine Analogy of faith, by which many Articles of the Apostles’ Creed, and very many Scriptural assertions concerning the nature of Christ’s Body, substantially like our bodies in all things. This Contradiction aimed at the Analogy of Faith is so far from being removed by miracles forged in this place that it is rather increased, inasmuch as it also infestively tears the Analogy of faith concerning the nature and scope of Miracles.
pass_b_english: (2) It clashes with the divine Analogy of faith — Creed articles and Scripture on Christ’s body as substantially like ours.
Forged miracles here do not heal that contradiction; they worsen it, tearing also the analogy of faith about what miracles are for.
source_text: (2.) Analogiæ fidei Divinæ, quà multos symboli Apostolici Articulos, plurimasque de Corporis Christi natura, nostris corporibus per omnia substantialia simili, Scripturæ assertiones. Contradictio hæc, Analogiæ Fidei intentata, usque adeò non tollitur per conficta hoc locô miracula, ut augeatur magis, quippe fidei quoque Analogiam, de Miraculorum natura ac scopo, infestans atque lacertans.

lemmas.gloss: to the divine Analogy of faith
